labels.label: prop:csc-yamabe
labels.notes: Unmarked, row partial: correct. csc_yamabe_a: R_g = c <= 0 (weakened to a.e.) gives EH = Y = c Vol^{2/N}, which is at least the paper's first assertion of (a). csc_yamabe_b: R_g = c > 0 and vol != 0 (nonemptiness, implicit in the paper) give 0 < Y <= EH. The Sobolev inequality is carried on a bare model and discharged sorry-free on a model reading a compact manifold (Mfd.Reads.csc_yamabe_b and prop_csc_yamabe). The uniqueness in (a) is a named Prop, CSCUnique: every positive weak solution of -a_N Lap u + R u = c' u^{p*-1} is a positive constant. It is a hypothesis hU, never an axiom, and the assembly only passes it through. That is disclosed, and toyClosed_cscUnique shows it is satisfiable, and not vacuously so: it is a real proof on the connected two-point model with R = 0. 'May be strict' is witnessed on the toy model (EH = 100*2^{2/3} >= 120 > 114 >= Y). I checked the arithmetic: dirichlet 1.62, a_3 = 8, R term 101, total 113.96, denominator >= 1. It is disclosed as a model fact; Schoen's S^1(L) x S^{N-1} is not formalized. FINDING CHECKED, correct. Line 161 defines closed as 'compact, without boundary', with no connectedness. On flat T^3 disjoint-union T^3, take u = 1 on one torus and u = 2 on the other. Then u^4 g is flat, has constant scalar curvature 0, lies in [g], and is not lambda*g for any single lambda. So the uniqueness as printed fails when R_g = 0 and Sigma is disconnected. For c < 0 every constant-curvature conformal factor is forced to the same constant on every component, so connectedness is not needed there. The REPORT says this correctly. toyClosedCut sets d := 0, so every function has zero gradient and zero Dirichlet energy. That is, each of the two points is its own component: a faithful model of a two-component closed Sigma. There u = (2,1), c' = 0 solves YamabeEq and is not constant. The REPORT phrases the finding 'as printed (no connectedness)' and asks whether Sigma is connected throughout section 2. That is the right framing, because many authors take manifolds to be connected by convention.
